note: Narrative prose only. See docs/BRITTAIN_SHAKESPEARE.md before remote use.

voice_author_death_years.note: Register comes from author life dates, NOT dcterms:issued. Gutenberg's issued date is its own release date - Dracula is stamped 1995 - so publication year is unavailable and would label the corpus Modern almost everywhere.

fiction_filter.note: A document must pass every rule. This is the control that keeps encyclopedic text out of an 80M-parameter story model.
fiction_filter.lcc_note: Literature classes only. Necessary but not sufficient: PR also holds poetry, criticism, and essays, so the subject exclusions and the dialogue floor still apply on top.
fiction_filter.floors_note: Speech OR verbs, not both. Drama is nearly all speech and has almost no narrative verbs (Hamlet: speech 0.248, verbs 0.0023), so an AND rule rejected Shakespeare. Speech counts quoted dialogue, drama speaker cues, stage directions, em-dash and single-quote conventions. Measured fiction speech p10=0.058 p50=0.255; verbs p10=0.0048 p50=0.0155.

world_texture.note: Narrative prose shelved under history, religion, or folklore: legends, folk tales, saints' lives, first-person war memoirs, Bible-story retellings. Setting texture for stories about the Crusades, a war, or a saint - NOT a route to encyclopedic knowledge. Capped so it cannot dilute, and gated by the text floors, which are what separate 'Tales and Legends of the English Lakes' from a regnal chronology.
world_texture.lcc_note: History, religion, folklore (GR), and general literature. Philosophy (B, BC, BD), psychology (BF), ethics (BJ), doctrinal theology (BT), and practical theology (BV) are deliberately absent: they are argument, not narrative.
world_texture.marker_note: biography is excluded from the fiction path but allowed here: saints' lives and first-person war memoirs are the most narrative material in these classes.
world_texture.exclusion_note: The relaxed 'biography' marker otherwise admits political autobiography, travel writing, linguistics references, and unit histories, all of which are expository.
world_texture.floors_note: Higher speech floor than fiction because these classes carry far more expository prose and their speech density is naturally lower (measured p50=0.089 against fiction's 0.255). Keeps about 66% of texture candidates; the 5% cap then binds.

windowing.note: Windows are cut at chapter or scene boundaries where detectable, else at paragraph boundaries. Never mid-sentence.

local_sources.name: early-modern
local_sources.note: Hand-assembled: Shakespeare, Marlowe, Jonson, Webster, and the KJV narrative books. The KJV needs book-level selection, which the per-file text floors cannot do, so the books are listed explicitly here.
local_sources.kjv_excluded_note: Leviticus and Deuteronomy are law, the Epistles are doctrinal argument, and the Psalms and Proverbs are poetry and wisdom. None are narrative, so none are included.

remote_sources.name: gutenberg-fiction
remote_sources.note: The official mirror, not a Hugging Face mirror. The HF mirrors generally ship text with the subject headings stripped, and the fiction filter and Genre tag both run on those headings.

remote_sources.name: standard-ebooks
remote_sources.note: Bulk downloads are gated behind Patrons Circle membership. The free route is cloning the per-book repositories. Optional at ~7% of the corpus.
